name: Landscape Design & Installation

objectives.text: Identify trees, shrubs, groundcovers, and flowers growing in a home or school landscape
Explain ways landscape plants serve people and creation, such as providing shade, blocking wind, feeding wildlife, and holding soil in place
Describe the steps of planting a tree or shrub correctly, including digging the hole, setting the plant at the right depth, backfilling, watering, and mulching
Measure a small outdoor area and sketch its boundaries and existing features on grid paper
Interpret common symbols and a legend on a simple landscape plan to identify the plants and structures it represents
Classify landscape plants by form, mature size, and function such as shade tree, screen, foundation shrub, or groundcover
Map the sunny, shady, wet, and dry areas of the school grounds to show where different plants would grow best
Create a labeled, to-scale landscape diagram using consistent symbols and measurements so another person could install from it
Identify common landscape plants by common and scientific names as practiced in the FFA Nursery and Landscape CDE
Explain how the elements of design, including line, form, texture, color, and scale, apply to landscape and ornamental plant systems
Demonstrate safe operation and care of landscape hand tools and power equipment used during installation
Conduct a site analysis that records existing features, utilities, drainage, sun exposure, views, and client needs
Develop a functional diagram that organizes a site into public, private, and service areas based on a client interview
Apply principles of design such as balance, focal point, unity, rhythm, and proportion to develop a landscape plan for a site
Select plants for specific locations on a site based on hardiness zone, light exposure, soil conditions, mature size, and intended function
Compare drafting tools and computer landscape design software and use them to produce a finished landscape plan
Demonstrate proper installation practices including bed preparation, planting balled-and-burlapped and container stock, staking, edging, and mulching
Explain the concept of landscape ecology and incorporate ecological practices such as native plantings, pollinator habitat, and rain gardens into a design
Plan hardscape features such as patios, walkways, and retaining walls by selecting materials and calculating quantities of pavers, base, and mulch
Prepare a cost estimate and bid for a landscape installation that itemizes plants, materials, equipment, and labor
Evaluate an existing landscape or landscape plan and propose specific improvements to its function, appearance, and sustainability
Develop an establishment care plan for a newly installed landscape that schedules irrigation, pruning, and fertilizer applications
Design and present to a client a complete landscape installation proposal that justifies plant selection, site conditions, budget, and long-term maintenance

changes: Kept all six original competencies, rewording a few for precision (planting steps now name key actions, design principles expanded, the grade 12 capstone reframed as a client proposal including budget). Added missing competencies across the span: purposes of landscaping, site measuring and sketching, plant classification by form and function, microclimate mapping, plant identification by scientific name for the Nursery and Landscape CDE, elements of design, tool and equipment safety, site analysis, functional area diagrams, plant selection by site conditions, drafting tools and software, installation practices, landscape ecology, hardscape planning and material quantities, cost estimating and bidding, design evaluation, and establishment care. Turf, floral, and controlled-environment content was left to the sibling sub-topics. Standards were attached only at grades 9 to 12 and only where an objective directly teaches the standard.
